title: lmcache/lmcache
summary: LMCache is a high-performance KV cache management layer that enables persistent, reusable, and tiered storage for LLM inference, significantly reducing TTFT and improving throughput for long-context and agentic workloads.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. It operates as a daemon process and requires network access to communicate with inference engines and storage backends (e.g., Redis). It handles sensitive model inference data, so it should be deployed within a secure, trusted network environment. The project is highly active and well-maintained.

title: openpipe/art
summary: ART (Agent Reinforcement Trainer) is a specialized framework for training multi-step LLM agents using GRPO, designed to improve agent reliability through reinforcement learning.
risk_notes: Installed via standard pip package. Requires integration with external services like Weights & Biases (W&B) for serverless training, necessitating API keys. The framework executes training logic which may involve significant compute resources and network access to model providers or inference clusters.

title: braedonsaunders/codeflow
summary: A browser-based codebase visualization and analysis tool that runs entirely client-side, offering dependency mapping, security scanning, and architectural health metrics.
risk_notes: The tool is exceptionally low-risk as it runs entirely in the browser using local client-side processing. If used with private GitHub repositories, it requires a GitHub Personal Access Token, which is stored only in browser memory and not persisted. It can be self-hosted by simply opening index.html, requiring no complex installation or elevated system permissions.

title: cassandra/home-information
summary: A centralized, spatial home management hub that integrates with existing self-hosted tools like Home Assistant, Frigate, and Paperless-ngx to organize home documentation, maintenance, and device control.
risk_notes: Uses a curl-to-bash install script which is a security anti-pattern. The application requires Docker and will likely need significant network access to communicate with other local services (Home Assistant, Frigate, etc.) and persistent storage access for document management. It is actively maintained but lacks a clear license, which may be a concern for some users.

title: loredcast/filewizard
summary: A self-hosted, browser-based utility that provides a unified interface for file conversion, OCR, and audio transcription by wrapping powerful CLI tools like FFmpeg, Pandoc, and Whisper.
risk_notes: The application is designed to be run via Docker, which is the recommended and safest deployment method. It wraps powerful system-level tools (LibreOffice, Pandoc, ImageMagick) and executes them; the author explicitly warns that exposing this publicly without OAuth/OIDC authentication poses a risk of arbitrary code execution. It requires persistent volume mounts for file processing, meaning it will have read/write access to the directories mapped to the container.

title: virgiliojr94/book-to-skill
summary: A powerful CLI tool that converts technical books and documentation into structured 'skills' for AI agents, enabling context-aware, low-token usage for tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.
risk_notes: Typically installed via Python/pip. It requires read access to your local files (PDFs/docs) and writes to specific agent configuration directories (e.g., ~/.claude/skills). It processes local data to generate structured markdown, which is then used by your LLM agent; ensure you are comfortable with the privacy implications of feeding your local documentation into your chosen AI provider's context.

title: vorssaint/vorssaint-utils
summary: A comprehensive, modular macOS menu bar utility that consolidates common system tools like volume mixing, system monitoring, window management, and app uninstallation into a single, privacy-focused application.
risk_notes: Distributed as a standard macOS application (likely .dmg or .zip). As a system-level utility, it requires extensive Accessibility and System Events permissions to perform window management, volume control, and input monitoring. It is open-source (GPL-3.0) and claims to be telemetry-free, but users should be aware that granting such broad permissions to a single binary carries inherent security risks.

title: maxvfischer/diy-cnc-machine
summary: A comprehensive, well-documented guide for building a DIY CNC machine from scratch using 3D-printed parts and standard electronics.
risk_notes: This is a hardware project involving physical assembly and electrical wiring. It requires manual assembly of high-voltage components and stepper motor drivers. No software installation risks (like sudo scripts) are present, but it involves physical safety considerations and potential fire hazards if wiring is done incorrectly.

title: clovalink/clovalink
summary: A high-performance, multi-tenant enterprise file management platform built with Rust and React, designed as a cost-effective, self-hosted alternative to services like Box or Dropbox.
risk_notes: Deployment is typically handled via Docker/Podman, which is standard and secure. It requires persistent storage (local or S3), a PostgreSQL database, and Redis. As a file management system, it will have access to all uploaded sensitive data and requires careful configuration of OIDC/SAML providers and network exposure.

title: bagelhole/devops-security-agent-skills
summary: A comprehensive library of structured, agent-ready knowledge base files (skills) designed to be consumed by AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor to automate DevOps, security, and infrastructure tasks.
risk_notes: The project is installed via 'npx' or git clone. It is essentially a collection of markdown files and scripts; it does not execute code itself but provides content for your AI agent to read. The primary risk is the 'agentic' nature of the tools consuming these files—if you grant an AI agent broad permissions (e.g., AWS/K8s access) and it follows these scripts, it could perform destructive actions. Always review the scripts before allowing an agent to execute them in a production environment.

title: agentfy-io/agentfy
summary: Agentfy is a modular multi-agent framework designed for social media automation, utilizing the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to orchestrate LLM-driven workflows across platforms like X, YouTube, and TikTok.
risk_notes: Requires standard Python environment (pip install). The application necessitates multiple sensitive API keys (OpenAI, X, YouTube, etc.) stored in a local .env file. It performs network-heavy operations and interacts with social media accounts, which carries risks of account suspension if automated actions violate platform terms of service.

title: voltagent/awesome-claude-skills
summary: A comprehensive, curated directory of official and community-contributed skills for AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.
risk_notes: This is a documentation/curation repository, not an executable tool itself. It provides links and configuration patterns for various agent platforms. Users should exercise caution when implementing third-party agent skills, as these often require API keys, filesystem access, and network permissions to function within your local development environment.

title: prat011/awesome-llm-skills
summary: A curated collection of 'skills' and workflow templates designed to extend the capabilities of AI agents like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and other LLM-based developer tools.
risk_notes: This is a documentation/curation repository, not executable software. It provides templates and instructions for configuring local skill directories. Risks are limited to the security posture of the AI agents you choose to run these skills with, which may have read/write access to your local filesystem and API keys.

title: microck/ordinary-claude-skills
summary: A comprehensive, community-aggregated collection of prompt-based skills and MCP-compatible tools for Claude, organized by category for easy integration into LLM workflows.
risk_notes: The repository is a collection of text-based prompt files and scripts. Installation involves cloning the repository and pointing an MCP server or Claude client to the local directory. The primary risk is executing arbitrary scripts or prompts from third-party sources; users should audit individual skill files before granting them access to sensitive local files or system commands via MCP.

title: capcom6/android-sms-gateway
summary: An open-source Android application that transforms a smartphone into a programmable SMS gateway, supporting REST API integration, webhooks, and end-to-end encryption.
risk_notes: Requires installing an APK on an Android device, which necessitates broad SMS and network permissions. It is actively maintained. Security risk is primarily tied to the exposure of the API endpoint if using a public cloud server; self-hosting the backend is recommended for privacy.

title: parthjadhav/app-store-screenshots
summary: A specialized AI agent skill that scaffolds a local Next.js-based editor for creating professional App Store and Google Play marketing screenshots.
risk_notes: Installed via 'npx skills' or manual git clone. It runs as a local Next.js development server on your machine. It requires filesystem access to read/write project files and images in your local directory. It does not inherently require external API keys unless integrated into a specific agent workflow, but it executes code locally within your development environment.

title: axtonliu/axton-obsidian-visual-skills
summary: A collection of prompt-based 'skills' for Claude Code that automate the generation of Obsidian Canvas, Excalidraw, and Mermaid diagrams from text.
risk_notes: Installs via Claude Code's plugin system, which executes prompts/skills within the Claude Code environment. It requires an active Claude Code setup and API access. The project is explicitly labeled as 'experimental' and the author notes that maintenance is not their primary focus, so users should expect potential bugs.

title: mengto/skills
summary: A curated library of structured 'agent skills' (Markdown-based playbooks) designed to improve the consistency and quality of outputs from AI coding agents like Cursor, Claude, and Codex.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository containing Markdown files and examples. It requires no installation, execution, or system permissions. It is safe to clone, though it relies on external AI services (Claude, Cursor, etc.) which may require their own API keys or subscriptions.

title: nyblnet/bento
summary: A self-contained, local-first office suite that stores documents as single, editable HTML files containing both the data and the application logic.
risk_notes: The project is browser-based and requires no installation; it uses the File System Access API to read/write local files. It is highly secure by design, offering a fully offline mode and E2EE for collaboration. The code is transparent, and the architecture avoids external dependencies or cloud lock-in.

title: silentchainai/silentchain
summary: A powerful Burp Suite extension that integrates various AI models (including local Ollama) for passive vulnerability analysis and security testing.
risk_notes: Installed as a Java extension (.jar) within Burp Suite. It requires access to your HTTP traffic and potentially your API keys (OpenAI, Claude, etc.) if not using local Ollama. It includes a built-in DataSanitizer to redact sensitive info before sending data to cloud providers, which is a positive security feature. Maintenance appears active.

title: arabelatso/skills-4-se
summary: A curated collection of over 180 structured 'skills' (prompts and procedural workflows) designed for Claude-based software engineering tasks, featuring a web-based manager for discovery and installation.
risk_notes: The project uses shell scripts (install.sh) for local deployment of the skills manager. Users should review these scripts before execution as they may modify local directories or environment configurations. As these are AI-driven prompts, they require active API keys for Claude/Anthropic and may interact with your local filesystem or codebase depending on how you integrate them into your workflow.

title: kennss/siliconscope
summary: A native macOS system monitor for Apple Silicon that provides deep visibility into Neural Engine, Media Engine, and memory bandwidth, with remote monitoring capabilities for Linux and other Macs.
risk_notes: Distributed as a standard macOS application (likely a .dmg or .app bundle). It requires system-level access to read hardware sensors and performance metrics, which is standard for system monitors. It includes a remote agent feature for monitoring other machines, which involves network communication. The project is actively maintained and uses native Swift/SwiftUI, reducing the risk associated with interpreted scripts or shell-based installers.

title: anmolsaini16/mapcn
summary: A set of ready-to-use, customizable React map components built on MapLibre GL and designed to integrate seamlessly with shadcn/ui.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/pnpm/yarn as a standard frontend dependency. It requires no elevated system permissions, but users should be aware of the CARTO Basemap terms of service regarding commercial usage and potential costs for tile providers.

title: tjboudreaux/cc-thinking-skills
summary: A collection of 28 structured reasoning and mental model frameworks designed to be used as 'skills' by AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
risk_notes: Installs via npx or manual file copying into local project directories. Since these are prompt-based skill definitions, they do not execute arbitrary code themselves but influence the behavior of your AI agent. Ensure your AI agent has restricted filesystem access if you are concerned about the agent executing the logic defined in these skills.

title: sync-in/server
summary: A modern, self-hosted alternative to Dropbox and Nextcloud, providing file storage, synchronization, and collaborative document editing with a focus on privacy and data sovereignty.
risk_notes: Distributed primarily via Docker, which is the recommended and safest installation method. Requires persistent access to local storage volumes and network ports. As a file-hosting platform, it handles sensitive user data and authentication credentials, necessitating proper firewall configuration and regular security updates.

title: nfzerox/virtualmaconipad
summary: A project enabling macOS virtualization on jailbroken M1/M2 iPads by leveraging modified hypervisor stacks.
risk_notes: Requires a jailbroken device, which inherently compromises the security model of iPadOS. Installation is performed via a custom Cydia/Sileo repository, granting the application elevated system-level permissions. The project relies on exploits and modified kernel components, posing significant stability and security risks.

title: pouzor/homelable
summary: A comprehensive self-hosted infrastructure visualization and monitoring tool that supports network scanning, rack layout design, and integration with Proxmox, Zigbee, and AI agents via MCP.
risk_notes: Distributed primarily as a Docker container or Proxmox LXC. Requires network-level access to perform scans (nmap) and read-only or read-write access to infrastructure APIs (Proxmox, MQTT/Zigbee2MQTT) to function effectively. The project is actively maintained and follows standard containerized deployment patterns.

title: kodiqa-solutions/vaults3
summary: A lightweight, single-binary S3-compatible object storage server designed as a modern, open-source alternative to MinIO, featuring built-in dashboard, encryption, and erasure coding.
risk_notes: Distributed as a single binary or via Docker. Requires filesystem access for data storage and network access for the S3 API and dashboard. As a storage server, it handles sensitive data and credentials; it should be run with restricted user permissions (not root) and behind a reverse proxy with TLS. The clustering features are marked as beta, suggesting caution for critical production data.

title: rawfilejson/awesome-osint-arsenal
summary: A massive, monolithic collection of over 750 security and OSINT tools with automated installation scripts.
risk_notes: The installation method relies on 'sudo bash' scripts which execute arbitrary code with root privileges across your entire system. This is a high-risk practice that can lead to system instability or compromise. Given the sheer volume of tools (750+), maintaining security and dependency integrity is impossible, and it is likely to clutter a system with conflicting packages.

title: geo-tp/esp32-bit-pirate
summary: A powerful, open-source multi-protocol firmware for ESP32 devices that functions as a versatile hardware hacking and debugging tool, similar to the Bus Pirate.
risk_notes: Firmware is installed via a web-based flasher (Web Serial API) or manual binary flashing. It requires physical access to hardware and provides low-level control over GPIO, radio, and network protocols. As a hardware hacking tool, it is designed to interact with external devices and should be used with caution regarding electrical safety and local network security.

title: suislanchez/polymarket-kalshi-weather-bot
summary: A sophisticated multi-strategy trading bot for Polymarket and Kalshi that uses ensemble weather forecasting and BTC microstructure analysis to identify market inefficiencies.
risk_notes: Requires API keys for Polymarket and Kalshi to execute trades, which grants the bot access to your financial accounts. The installation involves standard pip and npm workflows, but users should audit the code before providing exchange credentials. High number of open issues (68) suggests potential instability or maintenance lag.

title: nutlope/logocreator
summary: An open-source AI logo generator built with Next.js that leverages Flux models via Together AI, offering a clean implementation for brand asset creation.
risk_notes: Requires a Together AI API key to function. Installation is standard via pnpm/npm. The application is a web-based tool; it does not require root access or system-level permissions, but it does handle external API calls to third-party AI services.

title: databasus/databasus
summary: A robust, self-hosted database backup and recovery management platform featuring point-in-time recovery, automated restore verification, and multi-cloud storage support.
risk_notes: Distributed primarily as a Docker container, which is a standard and secure deployment method. It requires read-only access to your database and write access to your chosen storage backend (S3, local disk, etc.). Since it handles sensitive database credentials and encryption keys, it should be isolated in your network and managed via secure environment variables or a secret manager.

title: kaopu-xiaopu/web-design
summary: A Claude Code skill that enforces a 'spec-first' design workflow by generating a structured DESIGN.md file before producing web code from PRDs, URLs, or screenshots.
risk_notes: Installed by cloning into the local ~/.claude/skills/ directory. It requires Claude Code to be installed and configured with an Anthropic API key. As a Claude Code skill, it has the potential to read/write files in your project directory and execute scripts (like the included Playwright crawler) based on the instructions provided to the LLM.

title: ashishps1/awesome-engineering-articles
summary: A well-organized, curated list of high-quality engineering blog posts from major tech companies, categorized by company and topic to help developers learn about large-scale system design and architecture.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository containing markdown files. There is no code to execute, no installation required, and no security risk associated with accessing the content.

title: jordancoin/codemap
summary: A developer tool that generates structural dependency graphs and architectural context for AI coding agents, ensuring they understand project imports and blast radii without token-heavy file scanning.
risk_notes: Installs via Homebrew, Scoop, or direct binary download. Requires read access to the entire codebase to build dependency graphs. Integrates with local AI agent configurations (Claude Code, Codex) by modifying local project files (.codemap, .claude, .mcp.json). The tool is actively maintained and provides clear documentation on its integration hooks.

title: liquidslr/system-design-notes
summary: A comprehensive collection of study notes and curated resources covering system design principles and architecture patterns based on the popular Alex Xu books.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository containing Markdown files. There is no code to execute, no installation required, and no security risk associated with the content.

title: interceptsuite/proxybridge
summary: A cross-platform, process-aware proxy client that redirects TCP and UDP traffic through SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies, serving as a modern alternative to Proxifier.
risk_notes: Requires high-level system permissions (root/admin) to perform system-level traffic interception and packet filtering. The Linux installation method uses a 'curl | sudo bash' script, which is a significant security risk; manual inspection of the script or using the provided binary/package manager (Homebrew) is preferred. It has full visibility into network traffic for the processes it intercepts.

title: google-gemma/gemma-translator
summary: An offline, on-device voice translator project designed for Raspberry Pi 5, utilizing Gemma 4 and Moonshine for speech-to-text and translation.
risk_notes: The project uses shell scripts (setup.sh, deploy-pi.sh) that install system-level dependencies via apt and configure systemd services. It requires microphone and audio output access. It runs locally without external API keys, but the deployment script modifies system configurations (LXDE autostart, systemd), which should be reviewed before execution on a production machine.

title: alibaba-flyai/flyai-skill
summary: A CLI tool and agent skill that integrates Fliggy travel search capabilities directly into AI coding agents like Claude Code and OpenClaw.
risk_notes: Installs via npm (global or local). Requires network access to reach Fliggy/Alibaba APIs. Optional API key configuration is supported. As an agent skill, it executes within the context of your AI agent, meaning it can potentially pass data to the agent's LLM provider.

title: r44vc0rp/pgrok
summary: A self-hosted alternative to ngrok that uses SSH tunnels and Caddy to expose local services to the internet with automatic HTTPS.
risk_notes: Uses 'curl | bash' and 'curl | sudo bash' installation methods, which carry inherent security risks. Requires root access on the VPS to configure Caddy and systemd services. The tool manages SSH keys and exposes local ports to the public internet, requiring careful management of the VPS firewall and SSH configuration.

title: dorianborian/sesame-robot
summary: An open-source, 3D-printable quadruped robot project based on the ESP32, featuring a RESTful API, animation studio, and Python companion app for home-lab robotics integration.
risk_notes: Requires physical hardware assembly and soldering. Firmware is flashed via Arduino IDE. The robot connects to local WiFi and exposes a RESTful API; users should be aware of potential network exposure if the robot is accessible from outside the local network. No dangerous install scripts, but requires standard Python environment setup for the companion app.

title: formsmith746/sketchforge-3d
summary: A local-first, browser-based 3D CAD editor that supports STL/STEP workflows without cloud lock-in, offering both a standalone desktop app and a Docker-based self-hosting option.
risk_notes: The project is self-hosted via Docker or installed as a native macOS app. It is 'local-first,' meaning data stays in browser storage and does not require cloud accounts. The macOS app is unsigned, requiring a manual security bypass (xattr command) to run. As a browser-based tool, it relies on WebGL and standard browser security sandboxing.

title: raiyanyahya/how-to-train-your-gpt
summary: An exceptionally well-documented, step-by-step educational guide to building a modern LLM from scratch using PyTorch, focusing on LLaMA-style architecture.
risk_notes: The project is a set of Jupyter notebooks and Python scripts. It requires standard Python dependencies (PyTorch, etc.) via pip. It does not require root access or external API keys, as it is designed for local training/inference. The code is educational and transparent, posing minimal security risk.

title: 0xk3vin/megamemory
summary: An MCP server that provides persistent, graph-based memory for coding agents by storing project concepts and decisions in a local SQLite database.
risk_notes: Installed via 'npm install -g'. It runs as a local MCP server, meaning it has read/write access to the directories where your coding agent operates. It creates a '.megamemory' folder in your project root. It uses an in-process embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) which is downloaded automatically on first use. No external API keys are required for the core functionality, as it relies on the LLM provided by your MCP client.

title: alexandrosgounis/pdfx
summary: A desktop application built with Electron that allows users to bundle multiple PDF documents into a single, backwards-compatible PDF file using a custom JSON manifest.
risk_notes: Distributed as a pre-built binary or via source code (yarn). Requires local filesystem access to read/write PDFs. Optional AI features require user-provided API keys (Google, Anthropic, or OpenAI) stored in a local .dev.vars file. The project is actively maintained and uses standard web technologies.

title: rampstackco/claude-skills
summary: A comprehensive library of 103 modular 'Claude Skills' designed to standardize agent behavior across the web development lifecycle, from branding and SEO to dev-ops and QA.
risk_notes: Installed via Claude Code CLI using '/plugin install'. These skills act as system prompts/instructions for Claude; they do not execute arbitrary code on your machine directly, but they can guide Claude to perform actions on your filesystem or via connected MCP servers (like Ahrefs). Review the skill definitions before execution if you are concerned about the agent's behavior.

title: dronesploit/dronesploit
summary: A Metasploit-style CLI framework designed for pentesting and security research on light commercial drones.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires external dependencies like aircrack-ng to function. As a pentesting framework, it interacts directly with network interfaces and wireless protocols, requiring elevated privileges to perform packet injection or network manipulation. Actively maintained.

title: cosmicstack-labs/mercury-agent-skills
summary: A comprehensive, vendor-neutral registry of 'SKILL.md' playbooks designed to extend the capabilities of various AI agents and CLI tools.
risk_notes: The repository provides text-based skill definitions (SKILL.md) that are interpreted by third-party AI agents. The primary risk is the execution of arbitrary instructions by your chosen agent; users should review the content of any skill before execution. Installation is typically handled via the Mercury CLI or by manually placing files in local agent directories (~/.mercury/skills/). No root access or system-wide sudo commands are required for the registry itself.

title: armur-ai/pentest-swarm-ai
summary: An autonomous, swarm-based penetration testing framework that uses stigmergic coordination to orchestrate AI agents for recon, exploitation, and reporting.
risk_notes: High risk; this tool is designed to perform active exploitation against network targets. It requires API keys (Claude/OpenAI) and executes native security binaries (nmap, sqlmap). It should be run in a strictly isolated environment (e.g., a dedicated container or VM) to prevent accidental damage to production systems or unauthorized network activity. It is actively maintained and built in Go.

title: 1weiho/open-slide
summary: A React-based slide framework designed for AI coding agents to generate, iterate, and present slide decks using natural language prompts.
risk_notes: Installed via npx, which executes remote code. The project is a standard TypeScript/React monorepo using pnpm. It requires local filesystem access to generate and edit slide files. It is designed to integrate with AI agents (like Claude Code), which may require providing your own API keys to those agents to function as intended.

title: robbyant/lingbot-vision
summary: A collection of self-supervised Vision Transformer backbones optimized for dense spatial perception tasks like depth estimation and semantic segmentation.
risk_notes: Standard Python/PyTorch installation via pip. Requires a CUDA-capable GPU for practical inference. Downloads model weights from Hugging Face on first execution, which involves external network requests. No known security vulnerabilities, but requires standard dependency management practices.

title: microsoft/ai-engineering-coach
summary: A VS Code extension and GitHub Copilot canvas tool that analyzes local AI coding session logs to provide insights, track performance, and identify anti-patterns in AI-assisted development.
risk_notes: Requires manual build from source using npm and installation via VSIX. The tool accesses local AI session logs and workspace files to generate insights; the project documentation explicitly states that no data leaves the machine, which is a positive privacy signal. Maintenance is active by Microsoft.

title: nvidia/audio2face-3d
summary: A central hub for NVIDIA's Audio2Face-3D technology, providing SDKs, training frameworks, and plugins for integrating high-fidelity AI-driven facial animation into 3D pipelines.
risk_notes: Requires significant hardware resources (NVIDIA GPU recommended). Installation involves standard Docker containers or C++ SDK integration. No dangerous 'curl | sudo' patterns; however, it requires downloading large model weights from Hugging Face and potentially running high-compute inference workloads.

title: plugin87/ux-ui-agent-skills
summary: A comprehensive instruction and knowledge kit designed to turn Claude into a senior design architect, providing structured design tokens, accessibility auditing, and component engineering for various frameworks.
risk_notes: Installed via npm/npx, which executes JavaScript in your local environment. It functions as a knowledge layer for Claude Code or other LLM-powered IDEs, meaning it will have access to your project files and the context you provide to the LLM. It does not require root privileges, but it does interact with your local filesystem to generate code and design tokens.

title: open-gsd/gsd-pi
summary: A sophisticated terminal-based coding agent that integrates Git worktrees, project planning, and multi-LLM routing to automate software development lifecycles.
risk_notes: Installs via npm/npx, which is standard for Node.js tools but requires caution regarding dependency supply chain. The tool requires API keys for LLM providers and has broad filesystem access to manage Git repositories and project state in ~/.gsd/. It is actively maintained with frequent updates.

title: cmu-perceptual-computing-lab/openpose
summary: OpenPose is a industry-standard, real-time multi-person system for detecting human body, hand, facial, and foot keypoints.
risk_notes: Installation is complex, requiring manual compilation from source using CMake and handling dependencies like Caffe, OpenCV, and CUDA/OpenCL drivers. It requires significant GPU resources and access to camera hardware or video files. It is a well-established academic project, but maintenance is slower compared to modern Python-based AI libraries.

title: denislupookov/altersend
summary: A cross-platform, P2P file transfer utility that uses Hyperswarm DHT for direct, end-to-end encrypted transfers without cloud storage.
risk_notes: Installs via standard package managers (Homebrew, Flatpak, AUR) or official binaries. It requires network access for P2P discovery and filesystem access to send/receive files. The project is actively maintained and uses established P2P libraries (Hyperswarm).

title: plannotator/effective-html
summary: A collection of agent skills designed to help LLMs generate high-quality, self-contained HTML artifacts like wireframes, prototypes, and diagrams.
risk_notes: Installed via npx or specific agent plugins (Claude Code/Codex). It functions as a set of prompt-engineering templates and skill definitions for AI agents. It does not require root access or persistent background processes, but it does interact with the agent's context window and potentially local file system depending on the agent's capabilities.

title: ndolestudio/httpsms
summary: A robust SMS gateway solution that turns an Android device into an API-accessible SMS server, supporting webhooks and end-to-end encryption.
risk_notes: Requires self-hosting via Docker with dependencies on Firebase, SMTP, and Cloudflare Turnstile. The Android app requires SMS permissions. The system handles sensitive communication data, so secure configuration of the API and webhook endpoints is critical.

title: pixlcore/xyops
summary: A comprehensive, self-hosted workflow automation and server monitoring platform that integrates job scheduling, incident response, and real-time system observability.
risk_notes: Requires Node.js environment. As a system-level automation and monitoring tool, it inherently requires broad access to the host filesystem, network, and process management. It is designed for self-hosting, which necessitates careful configuration of its secret management and network exposure. The project is actively maintained with clear documentation on security and trust.

title: nasa-gibs/worldview
summary: An interactive web-based interface for browsing global, full-resolution satellite imagery provided by NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS).
risk_notes: Standard Node.js project installed via npm. Requires network access to fetch imagery tiles from NASA's public GIBS API. No sensitive local credentials or root access required. Maintained by NASA, ensuring high reliability and security standards.

title: itsfatduck/optimizerduck
summary: A popular, open-source Windows utility designed to improve system performance and privacy by automating common registry and system setting tweaks.
risk_notes: Distributed as a standalone .exe executable. Requires administrative privileges to modify system settings and registry keys. As with any system-level tweaker, it carries the risk of breaking OS functionality if used improperly; the project explicitly advises creating a system restore point before use.

title: aiming-lab/autoresearchclaw
summary: An advanced autonomous research agent framework that orchestrates multi-agent workflows to generate scientific papers, featuring human-in-the-loop controls and domain-specific execution agents.
risk_notes: Requires significant API key configuration (likely OpenAI/Anthropic/HuggingFace) to function. The framework executes code in sandboxed environments (Docker), which is a good security practice, but users should be cautious of the 'self-evolving' nature of the agents and ensure strict resource limits are set on the Docker containers to prevent runaway costs or unintended system access.

title: mtdvio/every-programmer-should-know
summary: A comprehensive, community-curated list of essential technical resources, concepts, and reading materials for software developers.
risk_notes: This is a documentation-only repository. There is no code to execute, install, or run, and it requires no system permissions or API keys. It is safe to browse.

title: gimanh/taskview-community

title: adrianhajdin/ai-resume-analyzer
summary: An educational project repository designed to accompany a YouTube tutorial on building a resume analyzer using React and the Puter.js SDK.
risk_notes: This is a boilerplate/tutorial project. It relies on Puter.js for backend services, which offloads authentication and data storage to a third-party platform. It is not a self-hosted solution in the traditional sense and lacks a production-ready security architecture.

title: wisher567/portpal
summary: A Tauri-based desktop dashboard that visualizes active network ports, identifies running development frameworks, and provides one-click process termination.
risk_notes: Distributed as native installers (.msi, .dmg, .deb). As a process manager, it requires elevated system permissions to inspect network sockets and terminate processes. Built with Tauri (Rust backend), which generally offers a smaller attack surface than Electron, but users should review the source code before running as it has full access to local process management.

title: stablyai/orca
summary: Orca is an AI-native IDE designed for orchestrating multiple parallel coding agents across isolated git worktrees, featuring deep integration with GitHub, Linear, and remote SSH environments.
risk_notes: Distributed as a desktop application (binary installer). Requires significant permissions to manage local files, execute shell commands, and access SSH keys for remote worktrees. It integrates with external AI providers and project management tools, requiring API keys or OAuth tokens. As an IDE, it has broad access to your codebase and environment.

title: hkuds/ai-trader
summary: AI-Trader is a platform designed to allow AI agents to trade, share signals, and participate in copy-trading communities.
risk_notes: The project requires connecting AI agents to an external third-party service (ai4trade.ai) via prompt-based registration. It handles financial data and potentially connects to broker APIs (Binance, Coinbase, Interactive Brokers). Self-hosting involves database configuration (PostgreSQL/SQLite) and likely requires managing sensitive API keys for market data and broker access. The lack of a clear license and the high-risk nature of automated trading agents make this a significant security and financial risk.

title: yifanfeng97/hyper-extract
summary: A powerful CLI and Python framework for transforming unstructured text into structured knowledge graphs and hypergraphs using LLMs.
risk_notes: Installed via pip. Requires API keys for LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) or local vLLM endpoints. It performs file system operations to read documents and write knowledge bases/Obsidian vaults. The project is actively maintained with frequent updates.

title: clucraft/priceghost
summary: A self-hosted price tracking application that uses a multi-strategy extraction system, including AI-assisted verification, to reliably monitor product prices across various e-commerce sites.
risk_notes: Requires API keys (Anthropic/OpenAI) or a local Ollama instance for optimal functionality. As a self-hosted TypeScript application, it likely runs via Docker or Node.js; users should review the Dockerfile/package.json for dependencies. It requires network access to scrape external websites, which may trigger anti-bot protections on target sites.

title: agents365-ai/drawio-skill
summary: A powerful agent-based tool that converts natural language, codebases, and infrastructure configurations into professional, editable draw.io diagrams.
risk_notes: The tool functions as an agent skill, typically integrated into LLM-based coding assistants like Claude Code or Cursor. It requires access to your local filesystem to parse codebases and infrastructure files (Terraform/K8s) to generate diagrams. It relies on the draw.io desktop CLI for rendering. Users should review the prompts sent to the LLM as they may contain sensitive architectural details or code snippets.

title: smaug6739/alexandrie
summary: A robust, self-hosted knowledge management platform that serves as a privacy-focused alternative to Notion and Obsidian, featuring multi-tenancy, OIDC support, and S3-compatible storage.
risk_notes: Installed via Docker Compose, which is a standard and secure practice. The application requires persistent storage volumes for data and S3-compatible storage for media. It handles sensitive user data and authentication, so it should be deployed behind a reverse proxy with TLS/SSL. The project is actively maintained and uses standard containerization.

title: martin-olivier/airgorah
summary: A Rust-based GUI tool for WiFi security auditing that leverages the aircrack-ng suite for packet capture and network analysis.
risk_notes: Requires root/sudo privileges via polkit for network interface management and packet injection. It is a native Linux application, installable via crates.io or AUR. Requires hardware with monitor mode support. Security posture is reasonable as it separates the GUI from the privileged agent.

title: vectifyai/openkb
summary: OpenKB is a CLI-based knowledge management system that compiles documents into a structured, interlinked wiki using LLMs, offering a vectorless alternative to traditional RAG.
risk_notes: Installs via pip; requires LLM API keys stored in a .env file. The web UI component runs a local server (default port 7566) which is unauthenticated by default, though it supports bearer token configuration. It requires filesystem access to read documents and write the compiled wiki.

title: tabularisdb/tabularis
summary: A modern, open-source cross-platform SQL workspace that supports a wide range of databases and includes built-in MCP server capabilities for AI agent integration.
risk_notes: Distributed as a desktop application via standard package managers (brew, snap, winget, flatpak). It requires network access to connect to databases and optional local AI model integration (Ollama). As a database client, it handles sensitive credentials and data; users should review the plugin system's security model if using third-party extensions.

title: danilo-znamerovszkij/draw-your-font
summary: A local-first Node.js CLI tool that converts photos of handwriting into professional-grade TTF/WOFF2 fonts using potrace for vectorization and optional Claude Code integration for labeling.
risk_notes: Installed via npx, which executes code directly from the npm registry. It requires local filesystem access to read image files and write font files. When used as a Claude Code skill, it may send image data to Anthropic's API for vision-based labeling, though the core CLI is deterministic and offline-capable.

title: diolinux/photogimp
summary: A configuration patch for GIMP that rearranges the UI and shortcuts to mimic Adobe Photoshop.
risk_notes: The installation involves manually overwriting local configuration files (~/.config/GIMP or %APPDATA%\GIMP). While it does not require root/sudo, it modifies user-level application settings and requires manual backup to avoid data loss. It is a static configuration patch rather than an active tool or automation pipeline.

title: zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill
summary: A structured framework for AI agents to perform reverse engineering and penetration testing tasks by providing standardized routing, toolchain bootstrapping, and workflow playbooks.
risk_notes: Requires cloning the repository and executing local PowerShell or Bash scripts to index tools. The project acts as a wrapper for powerful security tools (IDA, Frida, Ghidra, etc.) and will execute commands on your system based on AI agent instructions. It requires Java, Node.js, and Python environments. Users should exercise caution when allowing AI agents to execute automated scripts against binaries or network targets.

title: gregorojstersek/resources-to-become-a-great-engineering-leader
summary: A curated list of books, blogs, and newsletters focused on engineering leadership and system design.
risk_notes: This is a static documentation repository containing only links. There is no code to execute, install, or run, so there are no security risks associated with the repository itself.

title: ministackorg/ministack
summary: A lightweight, MIT-licensed alternative to LocalStack that provides a local AWS emulator for development and CI/CD pipelines.
risk_notes: Can be installed via pip or Docker. Running via Docker with -v /var/run/docker.sock allows the container to manage other containers on the host, which is a significant privilege. It is designed for local development and testing environments, not production exposure.
